item.title: Motorola can get Qualcomm to make improvements too. For Pixels, we regularly file issues reporting weaknesses and proposing improvements but have no special access and they often don't listen or prioritize the issues. Official support for GrapheneOS from Motorola resolves this.
item.content:encoded: Motorola can get Qualcomm to make improvements too. For Pixels, we regularly file issues reporting weaknesses and proposing improvements but have no special access and they often don't listen or prioritize the issues. Official support for GrapheneOS from Motorola resolves this.

item.title: Motorola is providing official support for GrapheneOS and has multiple engineers helping us port GrapheneOS to their devices and implement the required security features. We'll have what we need provided officially and can work with them to improve driver/firmware security too.
item.content:encoded: Motorola is providing official support for GrapheneOS and has multiple engineers helping us port GrapheneOS to their devices and implement the required security features. We'll have what we need provided officially and can work with them to improve driver/firmware security too.

item.title: Pixels used to be officially supported by the Android Open Source Project. Android 16 dropped Pixel support and they're now much harder to support than many other devices. We have to do a lot of reverse engineering and backport QPR1/QPR3 Pixel firmware/drivers for proper updates.
item.content:encoded: Pixels used to be officially supported by the Android Open Source Project. Android 16 dropped Pixel support and they're now much harder to support than many other devices. We have to do a lot of reverse engineering and backport QPR1/QPR3 Pixel firmware/drivers for proper updates.

item.title: Motorola Signature 27 meets all of our official security requirements. It provides a high performance hardware memory tagging (MTE) implementation from Qualcomm, a high quality dedicated secure element from NXP and we'll be able to provide 7 years of proper update from launch.
item.content:encoded: Motorola Signature 27 meets all of our official security requirements. It provides a high performance hardware memory tagging (MTE) implementation from Qualcomm, a high quality dedicated secure element from NXP and we'll be able to provide 7 years of proper update from launch.

item.title: It's a huge upgrade over a Pixel 11 Pro XL with far over double GPU performance, ~60% better single threaded CPU performance and ~80% better multithreaded CPU performance. It has significantly better cameras too.

item.title: We recently hired 4 experienced Android app developers to overhaul or replace each app included in GrapheneOS. The most recent hire starts at the end of this month. We shipped the Messaging app overhaul which is already far more usable, robust and secure but will get much better.

item.title: We expect the Pixel 11 series will ship firmware for MTE in Android 17 QPR2 since it's available in the QPR2 Beta releases. As long as it ships in the current form, we'll be able to support those. Most of the port from 6.12 to 6.18 is already done for those via our 10th gen port.
item.content:encoded: We expect the Pixel 11 series will ship firmware for MTE in Android 17 QPR2 since it's available in the QPR2 Beta releases. As long as it ships in the current form, we'll be able to support those. Most of the port from 6.12 to 6.18 is already done for those via our 10th gen port.

item.title: There are 0 additional changes required for porting the QPR2 drivers from 6.12 instead of 6.6, but most of the remaining patches needed adjustments.
item.content:encoded: There are 0 additional changes required for porting the QPR2 drivers from 6.12 instead of 6.6, but most of the remaining patches needed adjustments.We'll be porting the remaining Pixels from the Linux 6.1 LTS to 6.18. Those use a far different SoC but some work can be reused.

item.title: Our current 6.18 port is from the 6.6 branch currently used by the Pixel OS for those devices. We've also made a port from the 6.12 branch used in Android 17 QPR2 Beta to 6.18 too. Around 30% of the patches for our port are no longer be needed when starting from the QPR2 drivers.
item.content:encoded: Our current 6.18 port is from the 6.6 branch currently used by the Pixel OS for those devices. We've also made a port from the 6.12 branch used in Android 17 QPR2 Beta to 6.18 too. Around 30% of the patches for our port are no longer be needed when starting from the QPR2 drivers.

item.title: Note for users of #TDE[1] Preliminary Stable Builds (PSB).
item.content:encoded: Note for users of # Preliminary Stable Builds (PSB).As it is customary with every new # release, there is a short period of time when PSB packages will be held in a frozen state, matching the release ones. This facilitates switching back to stable package for those users who moved to PSB only for temporary reasons (for example for urgent fixes). Building of rolling PSB packages will resume on Nov 8, 2026.

item.content:encoded: Manpage Monday: bastille tagsOrganize your jails with labels.Tag two jails as prod at once> bastille tags 'myjail yourjail' add prodList every jail carrying the web tag> bastille tags ALL list webTags make it easy to target groups of jails across your fleet.> bastille service TAG nginx restart> bastille sysrc TAG -aeSee `man bastille-tags` for more details.
